Sure! Below is a **sample 7‑day itinerary** for a classic Paris vacation (feel free to tweak dates, activities, and budgets to suit your own style). I’ve grouped things by day, added some “must‑see” highlights, and sprinkled in practical tips so you’ll know how to get around, where to eat, and what to book in advance.

---

## Day 1 – Arrival & Settling In  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Arrive at Charles de Gaulle or Orly. Take the RER B train into the city center (or a taxi/ride‑share). Check into your hotel or Airbnb. |
| Afternoon | Grab a croissant & café au lait at a local boulangerie. Walk along the Seine to the Notre‑Dame area; enjoy the view from the Pont des Arts. |
| Evening | Dinner at a classic bistro in Le Marais (e.g., **Le Petit Fer à Cheval**). Stroll through the cobblestone streets, maybe stop for a glass of wine at a sidewalk bar. |

> **Tip:** If you’re staying near the Louvre, you’ll have easy access to many major sights on foot.

---

## Day 2 – Classic Landmarks  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Visit the Eiffel Tower early (book tickets online to skip lines). Take photos from Trocadéro Gardens. |
| Mid‑morning | Walk up Rue Cler market street for lunch—try a sandwich from **Boulangerie Poilâne**. |
| Afternoon | Head to the Arc de Triomphe; climb to the top for panoramic views. Then stroll down the Champs‑Élysées. |
| Evening | Sunset cruise on the Seine (buses or boats depart from near the Eiffel Tower). Dinner aboard or back at a riverside restaurant like **Le Jules Verne** (Michelin‑starred, optional splurge). |

> **Tip:** Book the Eiffel Tower tickets for a specific time slot 2–3 weeks ahead.

---

## Day 3 – Art & Culture  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Louvre Museum (arrive right when it opens to avoid crowds). Focus on the Denon Wing (Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo). |
| Lunch | Picnic in the Tuileries Garden (pick up baguette, cheese, charcuterie). |
| Afternoon | Musée d’Orsay (Impressionist masterpieces). |
| Evening | Explore Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye for dinner; try **Le Progrès** for a cozy atmosphere. |

> **Tip:** Buy a combined ticket for the Louvre + Musée d’Orsay to save time and money.

---

## Day 4 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Tram 12 to Montmartre. Walk up to Sacré‑Coeur; enjoy the view over Paris. |
| Mid‑morning | Wander the Place du Tertre; chat with artists. |
| Lunch | Try a crepe from **Creperie Josselin**. |
| Afternoon | Visit the Salvador Dalí Museum or the Espace Dalí. |
| Evening | Catch a cabaret show at Moulin Rouge or Lido (reserve seats in advance). |

> **Tip:** Wear comfortable shoes—Montmartre’s streets are steep and uneven.

---

## Day 5 – Day Trip Options  
Choose one based on your interests:

| Option | Highlights | How to Get There |
|--------|------------|------------------|
| Versailles | Palace, Hall of Mirrors, Gardens | RER C train to Versailles Château Rive Gauche (30 min). |
| Giverny | Monet’s House & Gardens | Train to Vernon, then bus/taxi to Giverny (45 min). |
| Champagne Region | Reims or Épernay vineyards | Train to Reims (45 min) + local tour. |

> **Tip:** For Versailles, buy a “skip‑the‑line” pass online. For Giverny, consider a guided tour that includes transport.

---

## Day 6 – Modern & Hidden Gems  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Pompidou Centre (modern art). |
| Lunch | Eat at **Café Constant** near the Eiffel Tower. |
| Afternoon | Explore Canal Saint‑Martin; pop into boutique shops and cafés. |
| Evening | Dinner in the Latin Quarter; try **Le Coupe Chou** for a romantic setting. |

> **Tip:** The Pompidou has free entry on the first Sunday of each month (if you’re flexible).

---

## Day 7 – Leisure & Departure  
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Relax at Luxembourg Gardens; maybe rent a bike or rowboat on the pond. |
| Lunch | Brunch at **Café de Flore** (iconic spot). |
| Early afternoon | Last‑minute souvenir shopping on Rue de Rivoli. |
| Late afternoon | Head back to your accommodation, collect luggage, and make your way to the airport. |

---

### Practical Tips & Booking Advice  

| Category | Recommendation |
|----------|----------------|
| **Accommodation** | Stay centrally (Marais, Latin Quarter, or near the Louvre) to minimize transit time. Look for hotels offering free Wi‑Fi and breakfast. |
| **Transportation** | Purchase a **Paris Visite** pass (valid for unlimited rides on Metro, RER, buses, trams). A 48‑hour pass often works well for a week‑long stay. |
| **Dining** | Reserve tables at popular restaurants (especially for Michelin‑starred places) at least 2–3 weeks in advance. |
| **Tickets** | Book major attractions (Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, Versailles) online to avoid queues. |
| **Language** | Learn a few basic French phrases (“Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Où est…?”). Most Parisians speak English in tourist areas, but locals appreciate effort. |
| **Safety** | Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded spots (metro, tourist sites). Use a money belt or anti‑thief bag. |
| **Weather** | Pack layers; Paris weather can be unpredictable. Bring a small umbrella and comfortable walking shoes. |

---

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a more tailored plan (budget, specific interests, longer stay, etc.) or if you need help booking tickets and accommodations!
